items.title: ROS Discourse General: ROS2 Dev Container Feature + Workspace Update
items.summary: A ROS2 Dev Container Feature was implemented, allowing users to select the ROS distro once in devcontainer.json and use the same configuration for local development and CI. The feature also updated VSCode ROS2 Workspace Template to use it instead of pre-built ROS Docker images. The main ROS distribution used is now "lyrical".
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS2 Dev Container Feature + Workspace Update," a new feature was implemented in ROS2 that allows users to select the ROS distro once in devcontainer.json and utilize the same configuration for local development and CI. This update also modified the VSCode ROS2 Workspace Template to use the ROS2 Dev Container instead of pre-built ROS Docker images, now leveraging the "lyrical" main distribution. The result is a streamlined process that simplifies user workflow and improves consistency in project setup across different environments.

items.audio_script:
From thehustle.co, "Cyborg roaches to the rescue?" Researchers from Nanyang Technological University (NTU) Singapore and Waseda University in Japan have developed a special diving suit for cyborg cockroaches to assist in search-and-rescue operations. The team successfully created these advanced insects, equipped with oxygen generation tanks and electronic controllers, allowing them to navigate underwater or on land for up to 3 hours. They can also withstand heavy rain, flooding, rubble, and narrow gaps. By leveraging biotechnology and robotics, the researchers have engineered a unique solution to aid in disaster response efforts.

The process involved integrating cutting-edge technologies into the roaches' bodies, including sensors, actuators, and power sources. The team employed a modular design approach, allowing for easy upgrades and customizations. Notably, the cyborg roaches were able to adapt to diverse environments, demonstrating their potential as effective search-and-rescue tools. Their ability to navigate through rubble or debris also opens up possibilities for exploration in challenging terrain.

This innovative development has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it showcases the intersection of biology and robotics. The successful creation of these cyborg roaches highlights the potential for future advancements in biologically-inspired technologies, which could lead to breakthroughs in search-and-rescue operations, environmental monitoring, and other fields.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Has a CPU shared-memory backend for rosidl::Buffer been explored?
items.summary: A CPU shared-memory backend for rosidl::Buffer has not been extensively explored, but some middleware and RMW implementations already provide shared-memory transport optimizations. Conceptually, a Buffer backend could use shared memory to store large variable-length payloads while making the payload storage itself shared, complementing transport-level shared memory rather than replacing it. There is currently no related work or design discussion that has explicitly explored this specific direction for rosidl::Buffer.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Has a CPU shared-memory backend for rosidl::Buffer been explored?" This discussion explores whether a CPU shared-memory backend for rosidl::Buffer has been extensively examined. Researchers and developers have already implemented middleware and Real-Time Middleware (RMW) optimizations that utilize shared memory to enhance transport efficiency, suggesting a potential path forward for improving the Buffer backend's performance. A conceptual framework could leverage shared memory to store large variable-length payloads while also making the payload storage itself shareable with transport-level shared memory, potentially offering benefits without replacing existing transport-level shared memory solutions. Currently, there is no concrete research or design discussion focusing on this specific direction for rosidl::Buffer.
